title: Augmentation comparison for the normalized DVR Roos object
statement: For a normalized DVR tower T, index n, chosen scalar-reduction adjunction, strict normalized adic tower U with level isomorphisms eU respecting successor maps, and countable products in the completed derived category, together with a finite-coefficient complex N, a chain isomorphism iN from U_(n+1) to its completed restriction and a finite-derived isomorphism eN:Q(N) to T.M n such that (eU n) followed by evaluationIso equals Q(iN), the restriction factor and Res(eN), there is a natural isomorphism from derived scalar extension followed by restriction to the localized scalar cone by the (n+1)-st uniformizer power. For the canonical homotopy-limit cone of U, its component at n+1, followed by the comparison and normalized cokernel descent, equals the restricted adjoint of the canonical Roos projection, after the supplied level isomorphism and evaluation isomorphism. The scalar-cone functor and augmentation are [def-coef-linear-scalar-cone]; T is [def-coef-normalized-dvr-tower], strict normalization is [lem-coef-strict-normalized-adic-cone-limit], the adjunction is [lem-weil-derived-scalar-extension-restriction-adjunction].

proof.text: Use the strict finite-coefficient adjoint formula, including its natural comparison for the specified adjunction, on the normalized reduction from the zeroth tail term followed by iN.

The normalized cokernel descent gives the reduction on the unshifted summand and zero on the shifted summand. The finite coefficient compatibility identifies the target via eN; right adjunction naturality proves the formula on the zeroth tail term. Left adjunction naturality and naturality of the comparison transport it along the canonical homotopy-limit projection. Cone naturality identifies this projection followed by the normalized reduction with the level n+1 projection.

theorem normalizedDVR_roos_augmentation
    (T : NormalizedDVRTower l E X D hl) (n : ℕ)
    (adj : scalarReductionDerivedExtension l E X n ⊣
      scalarReductionDerivedRestriction l E X n)
    [HasLimitsOfShape (Discrete ℕ) (completedIntegralDerivedCategory l E X D hl)]
    (U : ℕᵒᵖ ⥤ CochainComplex (completedIntegralModuleSheaves l E X D hl) ℤ)
    (hU : CochainComplex.IsNormalizedAdicTower (normalizedDVRUniformizer l E X) U)
    (eU : ∀ j : ℕ, DerivedCategory.Q.obj (U.obj (op (j + 1))) ≅
      (normalizedDVRTowerEvaluation l E X D hl j).obj T.tower)
    (_heU : ∀ j : ℕ,
      DerivedCategory.Q.map (U.map (homOfLE (Nat.succ_le_succ j.le_succ)).op) ≫
          (eU j).hom = (eU (j + 1)).hom ≫
        (normalizedDVRTowerTransition l E X D hl j.le_succ).app T.tower)
    (N : CochainComplex (normalizedDVRModules l E X n) ℤ)
    (iN : U.obj (op (n + 1)) ≅
      ((completedIntegralRestrictScalars l E X D hl n).mapHomologicalComplex
        (.up ℤ)).obj N)
    (eN : (@DerivedCategory.Q _ _ _ (HasDerivedCategory.standard _)).obj N ≅ T.M n)
    (hN : (eU n).hom ≫ (T.evaluationIso n).hom =
      DerivedCategory.Q.map iN.hom ≫
        (completedIntegralRestrictScalars l E X D hl n).mapDerivedCategoryFactors.inv.app N ≫
        (normalizedDVRResCompleted l E X D hl n).map eN.hom) :
    ∃ A : scalarReductionDerivedExtension l E X n ⋙
          scalarReductionDerivedRestriction l E X n ≅
        CochainComplex.LinearScalarCone.derived
          (A := completedIntegralModuleSheaves l E X D hl)
          (normalizedDVRUniformizer l E X ^ (n + 1)),
      let c := CategoryTheory.Pretriangulated.homotopyLimitCone (U ⋙ DerivedCategory.Q)
      let k := (CategoryTheory.Pretriangulated.addOpFunctor (n + 1)).obj (op 0)
      (scalarReductionDerivedRestriction l E X n).map
          ((adj.homEquiv c.pt (T.M n)).symm
            (c.π.app (op (n + 1)) ≫ (eU n).hom ≫ (T.evaluationIso n).hom)) =
        A.hom.app c.pt ≫
          (CochainComplex.LinearScalarCone.derived
            (normalizedDVRUniformizer l E X ^ (n + 1))).map (c.π.app k) ≫
          CochainComplex.LinearScalarCone.derivedAugmentation hU (n + 1) (op 0) ≫
          (eU n).hom ≫
          (T.evaluationIso n).hom

statement_change.what: Completed-derived successor compatibility alone does not preserve the finite coefficient action. For R a DVR, twist eU_0 on B_1 direct-sum B_1[1] by the nonzero Bockstein B_1 -> B_1[1] and leave higher level comparisons canonical. Precomposition with B_2 -> B_1 kills this Bockstein, so successor compatibility remains. The limit is R direct-sum R[1] and its projection kills the twist, while the cone augmentation sees it. Naturality with summand idempotents prevents a natural comparison from absorbing this off-diagonal twist. Require the selected level comparison to arise from a strict finite-coefficient complex and a finite-derived isomorphism instead. The canonical finiteModel supplies this.
